text:
Jamie Benn has been one point from 1,000 since last weekend, and Thursday's 8-3 loss to Winnipeg was nobody's idea of the night to get there. He gets another chance at home against Buffalo. Benn has spent all 1,269 of his NHL games with Dallas, and he'd be only the second player to reach 1,000 points with the franchise, after Mike Modano, per NHL.com. At 37 the captain has seven points in 17 games this season, so the milestone has taken some waiting.

The Stars have more pressing worries than the wait. Miro Heiskanen is out with an upper-body injury (ESPN estimates Nov. 17), and Daily Faceoff reported Friday that Lian Bichsel will miss at least two weeks. Thomas Harley has moved onto the first power-play unit and Tyler Myers is playing 20:30 a night, up from 17:10. Jake Oettinger, our projected starter, has stopped .842 over his last five starts, 4.3 goals worse than expected. Wyatt Johnston hasn't scored in five games on 3.0 expected goals, a drought the chances say isn't on him. Tyler Seguin, now a third-liner, is one of our Sleepers.

Buffalo is winless in three, including an 8-3 loss in Tampa where Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen was pulled and Tage Thompson called out what Heavy.com described as a troubling pattern. Then came a 3-2 overtime loss in Chicago, Alex Lyon's season debut. The Sabres have a minus-12 goal difference on chances that are almost even (minus-0.4), so they have both missed chances and allowed too many: 6.5 goals short on finishing, 5.1 goals allowed above expected. Luukkonen is projected to start again. Thompson is one assist from 200 for his career and Jack Quinn one from 100.

Both teams take about four penalties a game, so watch the special teams: Dallas's power play creates 0.79 expected goals a game, and Buffalo's penalty kill allows 0.77. Our numbers have the Stars at 3.17 expected goals to Buffalo's 2.78, and Dallas at 75% to make the playoffs against Buffalo's 26%. The only meeting so far went 4-0 to Dallas on Oct. 8.
headline: Jamie Benn sits one point from 1,000
